This appeal is filed by Iffco Tokio General Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 09.08.2021 passed in MVC No.671/2019 on the file of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Ranebennur (for short, 'Tribunal'), questioning the liability NC:

sentences.text: Tribunal.

2. Brief facts giving raise to filing of this appeal are that the claimants, who are the legal heirs of deceased Manjunath Enigi, have filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 seeking compensation in respect of death of Sri.Manjunath Enigi in a road traffic accident that took place on 20.01.2019 at 19.00 hours.
It is averred that on the date of accident, i.e., on 20.01.2019, the deceased was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA-34/E-1576 from Madalagatta to Hadagali on Hadagali-Mundaragi road.
When he reached near Kombli village, one TATA Ace bearing No.KA-34/B-1015 came from opposite direction in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the deceased.
As a result, Manjunath Enigi sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
It is averred that the deceased was mason and doing coolie work, earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
It is further averred that the entire NC: 2023:KHC-D:7485-DB family was depending on the income of the deceased.

It is also averred that after completion of investigation, the investigating officer filed charge sheet against the driver of TATA Ace vehicle and hence, respondent No.3 the registered owner of TATA Ace vehicle and respondent No.2 insurer of TATA ACE vehicle are responsible for payment of compensation.
3.
Respondent No.3 was placed exparte before the Tribunal.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 entered appearance.
Respondent No.2-insurance company filed written statement denying the averments of the claim petition.
It is averred that the vehicle was insured for a period from 10.07.2018 to 09.07.2019.
It is further averred that there is no nexus between the accidental injuries and death of the deceased.
It is also averred that the respondent Nos.1 and 3 violated the policy conditions.
Therefore, the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.
4. The Tribunal has framed issues and recorded the evidence of the parties.
The respondent No.1 NC: 2023:KHC-D:7485-DB examined herself as PW-1 and got marked 14 documents at Exs.P-1 to P-14.
The respondent examined RW-1 and got marked two documents at Exs.R-1 and R-2.

The Tribunal based on the material evidence on record, has allowed the claim petition awarding compensation of Rs.29,01,296/- with interest at 9% p.a.
5.

Learned counsel Sri Ravindra R. Mane for appellant-insurance company submits that the Tribunal has failed to consider that the offending vehicle TATA ACE bearing No.KA-34/B-1015 insured with the appellant was not having valid fitness certificate as on the date of accident and the said vehicle was not roadworthy, hence, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the said vehicle.
He further submits that the Tribunal has erred in fastening the liability on the appellant insurance company instead on the owner of the offending vehicle.

It is also submitted that to substantiate the defence of the appellant before the Tribunal, it has examined official of the appellant as RW-1 and got marked two documents and NC: 2023:KHC-D:7485-DB without appreciating the evidence on record, the Tribunal has proceeded to saddle the liability on the appellant- insurance company instead of respondent No.6 owner of the vehicle.

It is submitted that the award of compensation by the Tribunal is just and proper however award of interest at 9% per annum on the compensation amount is exorbitant and on higher side, requires to be interfered in this appeal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 6. Per contra, learned counsel Sri Chandrashekhar Hosamani for respondent Nos.1 to 5/claimants,

learned counsel Sri Madanmohan M. Khannur for respondent No.6 owner of the vehicle support the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal. It is submitted that the Tribunal on considering the evidence on record has fastened the liability on the insurance company, the same does not call for any interference in this appeal.
7. We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant insurance company, learned counsels for the NC: 2023:KHC-D:7485-DB respondents, perused the memorandum of appeal and Tribunal records.
8. The points that arise for consideration in the appeal are (1) Whether the Tribunal is justified in fastening the liability on the appellant-insurance company?
(2) Whether the Tribunal is justified in awarding interest at the rate of 9% per annum?

9. The answer to the above point No.1 is in the affirmative and point No.2 is in the negative for the following reasons;
10.
There is no dispute with regard to the accident and the death of Manjunath Enigi in the road accident dated 20.01.2019.
The Tribunal considering the evidence on record, has awarded compensation of Rs.29,01,296/- with 9% interest per annum from the date of petition till realisation.

While awarding compensation, the Tribunal has fastened the liability on the appellant insurance company on the ground that the offending vehicle was NC: 2023:KHC-D:7485-DB insured with the appellant insurance company.
The appellant-insurance company has contended that as on the date of accident, the offending vehicle TATA ACE bearing No.KA-34/B-1015 was not having the fitness certificate.
Hence, the appellant-insurance company is not liable to pay compensation and not liable to indemnify the offending vehicle.
The issue raised in this appeal is no more res integra.

The Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs.
Kumar and others in M.F.A.No.7792/2015 c/w M.F.A.No.6449/2015 vide judgment dated 21.12.2020 has held that even if no valid fitness certificate as on the date of accident it is not the defence available for the insurance company under Section 149(2) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 and it is not a condition which is mentioned in the policy, but it is only an offence under the Motor Vehicle Act and the insurance company cannot escape from liability.

entities.text:
Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs.
Kumar and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Co-Ordinate Bench has considered the issue of valid fitness certificate from paragraph 12 to paragraph 24 in the judgment referred NC: 2023:KHC-D:7485-DB supra and held that the contention of the insurance company that the insured has violated the policy condition and the insurer is not liable to pay compensation is unsustainable, the insurance company is held liable to indemnify the insured and the insurance company was directed to pay compensation along with the interest.
We have gone through the judgment referred supra, we are in full agreement with the reasons assigned in the said judgment by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court.

In view of the settled position of law, we hold that even the fitness certificate is not valid on the date of accident, it is an offence under the Motor Vehicle Act,
liable for penalty and the insurance company has no defence, hence, they are liable to indemnify the insured and liable to pay the compensation.
In the instant case, the offending vehicle was insured with the appellant and the policy was in force.
Hence, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation as awarded by the Tribunal.

4 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7485-DB 11.

entities.text: Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co Ltd vs Smt. H Lakshmi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has committed an error in awarding 9% interest on the compensation amount.
This Court is of the considered view that award of interest at 9% is on high sides.
Keeping in mind the present rate of interest paid by the Nationalized Banks on the term deposits, it would be appropriate if 6% interest is awarded on the compensation amount instead of 9%.

12. For the aforementioned reasons, we pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The judgment and award dated 09.08.2021 passed in MVC No.671/2019 on the file of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Ranebennur is modified to the extent that the appellant is directed to pay compensation amount of Rs.29,01,296/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7485-DB (iii) The registry is directed to transmit the amount in deposit to the Tribunal along with records.
 (iv) Draw the decree accordingly.
